key_concepts: Friction is a force between two surfaces in contact or rubbing.
Friction acts opposite the direction of applied force and slows moving objects.
Rough surfaces create more friction; smooth surfaces create less.
The four types of friction are static, sliding, rolling, and fluid.
Static friction acts on resting objects and is strongest between solid surfaces.

Fluid friction, or drag, occurs when objects move through liquids or air.
Surface texture, normal force, and surface area affect friction.
